messages.content: Let's go back to Washington for fall break. The two windows are Friday, October 10 through Tuesday the 14th, or Saturday the 11th through Wednesday the 15th. I need actual four-night comparisons, not just nightly rates.

I can compare representative air-and-hotel packages for all three areas. I’ll include mandatory lodging charges and taxes, and I’ll only use room types that state occupancy for three. Are you comfortable using DCA for the comparison, or should I include IAD and BWI?
Use DCA. There are three of us flying from Dallas, and I don't want to add a long airport transfer to save a little on airfare.

Understood. For a planning snapshot, the Friday-to-Tuesday nonstop round trips are about $1,167 total for three, while Saturday-to-Wednesday is about $957 total. Both examples use DFW-DCA economy flights with normal daytime schedules. Those are representative fares, not held prices.
Now pair those with one hotel near the Mall, one in Penn Quarter, and one in Dupont. Make sure the room really allows two adults and a 14-year-old.

For each property I used a two-queen room explicitly listed for three guests. Near the Mall, Holiday Inn Washington Capitol-National Mall comes to about $1,136 for four nights: $980 room charge plus approximately $156 tax, with no separate mandatory property fee shown. In Penn Quarter, Riggs Washington DC comes to about $1,503: $1,156 room charge, $140 mandatory guest amenity fees, and about $207 tax. In Dupont Circle, The Royal Sonesta Washington DC Dupont Circle comes to about $1,164: $876 room charge, $128 mandatory destination fees, and about $160 tax.
Are those hotel numbers the same for both date patterns?

Not exactly. Those are the Friday-to-Tuesday examples. For Saturday-to-Wednesday, the representative four-night totals are approximately $1,090 at Holiday Inn Capitol, $1,456 at Riggs, and $1,126 at Royal Sonesta. The later window avoids the higher Friday night at each property.
Give me the complete package totals for all six combinations.

Friday October 10 to Tuesday October 14: Holiday Inn Capitol plus flights is about $2,303; Riggs plus flights is about $2,670; Royal Sonesta plus flights is about $2,331. Saturday October 11 to Wednesday October 15: Holiday Inn Capitol plus flights is about $2,047; Riggs plus flights is about $2,413; Royal Sonesta plus flights is about $2,083. These totals cover three round-trip airfares and one room for four nights, including the hotel taxes and mandatory fees identified above. They exclude checked bags, airport transportation, parking, meals, and optional hotel purchases.
So Saturday saves more than I expected. Is there any sightseeing penalty besides losing Friday evening?

The main issue is museum timing. With Saturday arrival, you would have Sunday through Tuesday as full sightseeing days and Wednesday morning before departure. That still fits the Smithsonian museums, Capitol area, and Georgetown, but it compresses the plan if you want several museums rather than two or three. Friday arrival gives you four usable daytime blocks from Saturday through Tuesday if the return is late enough.
Show me how the neighborhood changes those days. Assume Air and Space, Natural History, the Capitol area, and one afternoon in Georgetown.

From Holiday Inn Capitol, Air and Space is roughly a 5-minute walk, Natural History about 15 minutes, and the Capitol grounds around 15 minutes. That location makes the museum and Capitol days easiest, but Georgetown generally requires a Metro-plus-walk, bus, or rideshare. From Riggs, Natural History is about a 10-minute walk, Air and Space about 18 minutes, and the Capitol about 20 minutes; it also gives you convenient Metro access for Georgetown. From Royal Sonesta, Georgetown is the easiest outing at roughly 20 to 25 minutes on foot, while the museums and Capitol require Metro or a longer walk.
Could the Saturday schedule work without putting two major museums on the same day? My daughter will be done if we try that.

Yes. Saturday can be arrival and a light evening. Sunday: Air and Space, with the rest of the day around the Mall. Monday: Capitol area, including a timed Capitol tour if available. Tuesday: Natural History in the morning and Georgetown after lunch. Wednesday can remain breakfast and departure. That keeps the two major museums on separate days, although Tuesday is still the busiest day because it crosses the city.
And for the Friday window?

Friday can be arrival only. Saturday: Air and Space. Sunday: Natural History. Monday: Capitol area. Tuesday: Georgetown before an evening flight. It is better paced, but the Georgetown plan depends on having a return late enough to retrieve luggage and reach DCA without rushing.
I don't love putting Georgetown on departure day. Move it if we stay near the Mall.

For the Friday window at Holiday Inn Capitol, use Saturday for Air and Space, Sunday for Georgetown, Monday for the Capitol area, and Tuesday for Natural History before departure. For the Saturday window, use Sunday for Air and Space, Monday for the Capitol, and Tuesday for Natural History followed by Georgetown. The later window cannot fully separate all four items because it only has three complete sightseeing days.
Which package is the sensible value, considering both cost and transit?

The Saturday-to-Wednesday Holiday Inn Capitol package is the strongest value at about $2,047. It is approximately $36 less than the Dupont package and $366 less than Penn Quarter, while placing three of your four priorities within walking distance. Dupont only becomes the better fit if making Georgetown easier matters more than taking Metro or rideshares to every Mall and Capitol day. Riggs is the most central compromise, but the $140 mandatory amenity charge makes its package hard to justify on price.
Before I lean that way, tell me what is solid and what needs verification. I don't want an amenity surprise or a room that only sleeps two on paper.

For comparison purposes, the Saturday-to-Wednesday Holiday Inn package is about $2,047: roughly $957 for three nonstop DFW-DCA tickets and $1,090 for a four-night two-queen room. The location supports the proposed three-day sightseeing schedule, and no separate mandatory property fee appeared in the representative rate. Before selecting it, verify live airfare and schedules, baggage costs, the hotel’s final taxed total, that the exact room is bookable for two adults and one 14-year-old, and that no destination, facility, or other mandatory fee is collected at check-in. Also check the cancellation deadline and secure timed entry for Air and Space and the Capitol tour. Nothing has been booked.
